title: Mild Cajun Chicken Rigatoni (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo on Pexels (Pexels License)
creator: Vanessa Cooks
summary: Viral creamy Cajun chicken rigatoni vibe from Vanessa Cooks — adapted for no heat, high protein, and lower carb/cal while keeping the smoky-creamy pasta night energy.
whyItFits: Big flavor without cayenne / chili heat
Easy to push protein and dial pasta down

items: Skip cayenne / chili powder / hot Cajun packets
1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken breast, bite-size pieces (bump from ~1 lb for protein)
8–10 oz protein rigatoni / penne (Barilla Protein+, chickpea, or similar) — not a full 16 oz box
1/2 cup half-and-half or light cream (lighter than full heavy cream)
1/2 cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt (stir in off heat)
3/4–1 cup shredded part-skim cheddar or mozzarella
Optional: big handful baby spinach at the end

steps: Mix the mild Cajun blend. Boil salted water; cook pasta until just al dente. Drain, reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Toss chicken with 1 tbsp of the blend + a pinch of salt. Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken until browned and 165°F, ~5–7 min. Remove to a plate.
In the same pan, sauté onion and bell pepper ~4 min until soft. Add garlic 30–60 sec.
Sprinkle in remaining blend (~2 tbsp); stir 20 sec. Deglaze with chicken broth, scraping the pan. Stir in half-and-half / light cream; gentle simmer 2–3 min until slightly thick.
Return chicken. Add drained pasta. Off heat (or on warm only), stir in Greek yogurt, cheddar, and Parmesan until creamy. Loosen with pasta water. Fold in spinach if using.
Taste — add salt/pepper, not heat. Finish with parsley.
substitutions: No spice: homemade blend above; never use store “Cajun” mixes that lead with cayenne unless you verify the label.
Lower carb: 6–8 oz protein pasta + zucchini noodles or extra peppers; keep the full chicken amount.
Higher protein: 2 lb chicken; serve with a side of Greek yogurt “garlic dip” (yogurt + garlic powder + parsley).
Sweeter sauce note (optional): a tiny pinch of granulated stevia or a splash of 0-sugar simple syrup if the peppers taste sharp — usually not needed.
Dairy-light: more broth + yogurt, less cream; cheese can drop to 1/2 cup.
notes: Extra chicken, protein pasta, light cream + Greek yogurt finish, cayenne-free seasoning.
Facebook reel: full on-screen method wasn’t extractable behind login; this matches the common creamy Cajun chicken rigatoni pattern for that Vanessa Cooks title.
If you want it closer to the video after you watch it again, send any on-screen ingredients and we’ll tweak.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate ~480–550 kcal · ~45–55g protein · ~35–45g carbs · ~14–20g fat; varies with pasta brand and cheese.

title: Mild Sweet & Sticky Chicken (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo on Pexels (Pexels License)
creator: foodiligence
summary: Viral Sweet and Sticky Chicken from foodiligence (Ep 11). Adapted for no spice, high protein, and your sweetener kit while keeping the glossy Asian-style glaze.
whyItFits: Easy over cauliflower rice / a small rice scoop + extra veg

items: 16–24 oz boneless skinless chicken thighs, bite-size (start at 16 oz like the reel; bump to 1½ lb for more protein)
Or chicken breast if you want leaner — don’t overcook
2–3 tbsp cornstarch (light coat for crisp edges)

ingredients.section: Sticky glaze (no real sugar, no heat)
items: ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce or tamari
2–3 tbsp 0-sugar simple syrup (sucralose) or 1–2 tbsp granulated stevia + 2 tbsp water (taste as you go — brands vary)
Optional depth: 2–4 drops monk fruit extract instead of / with stevia
1 tsp grated fresh ginger or ½ tsp ginger paste
1 tbsp rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar
2–3 tbsp water or low-sodium chicken broth
Skip chili flakes, sriracha, sweet chili sauce (those add heat)
Serve with: cauliflower rice, a small scoop of jasmine rice, steamed broccoli, or cucumber salad

steps: Pat chicken dry. Toss with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and cornstarch until lightly coated.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook chicken in batches until golden and 165°F, ~3–4 min per side. Don’t crowd. Set aside.
Lower heat to medium. In the same pan, sauté garlic (+ ginger) ~30 sec. Stir in soy, sweetener syrup/stevia mix, vinegar, and water/broth. Simmer 1–2 min until glossy and slightly thick.
Return chicken; toss until every piece is lacquered and sticky, 1–2 min. If too thick, splash water; if thin, simmer another minute.
Kill heat; drizzle sesame oil. Top with sesame seeds and green onions.
substitutions: Sweeteners: 0-sugar simple syrup is the easiest 1:1 honey stand-in for stickiness; stevia/monk fruit work but start low and adjust — too much tastes bitter.
No spice: never add chili / sweet-chili / gochujang; smoky depth can come from a pinch of smoked paprika if you want (optional).
Lower carb: cauliflower rice or zucchini noodles; keep full chicken amount.
Higher protein: 1½–2 lb chicken; same sauce volume is fine.
Crispier: air-fry cornstarch-coated pieces at ~400°F until browned, then toss in the skillet glaze.
notes: Thighs or breast, cornstarch light coat, honey swapped for zero-sugar sweeteners, no chili heat.
Facebook caption truncated after the chicken line; method matches the common viral sweet-sticky chicken-bites pattern for this title.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate chicken only ~280–380 kcal · ~35–45g protein; depends on thigh vs breast and sweetener.

title: Mild Beef & Broccoli (Justin cut)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Mohamed Olwy on Pexels (Pexels License)
creator: foodiligence
summary: Viral Beef and Broccoli from foodiligence (Ep 21). Classic takeout-style stir-fry, adapted for no heat, high protein, and lower carb/cal — still glossy and savory.

items: 1–1.25 lb flank, sirloin, or flat iron, sliced thin against the grain (bump from ~¾–1 lb for protein)
1 tbsp low-sodium soy sauce or tamari
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry or extra broth
Sweetener: pinch granulated stevia or ½–1 tsp 0-sugar simple syrup (instead of sugar)
3–4 tbsp water or low-sodium beef/chicken broth
Skip chili oil, chili flakes, white pepper heat if sensitive — black pepper optional and light
1 medium head broccoli (~10–12 oz), cut into florets (big pile)
Optional: few slices onion or a handful mushrooms
Cauliflower rice, or a small scoop jasmine rice / protein noodles

steps: Slice beef thin against the grain. Toss with baking soda, soy, water, cornstarch, oil; rest 15 min.
Whisk sauce ingredients (except sesame oil) in a small bowl.
Blanch or microwave broccoli until bright green and just tender-crisp (1–2 min boil or ~2 min microwave with splash of water). Drain well.
Heat a wok/skillet screaming hot with 1 tbsp oil. Sear beef in a single layer in batches, ~45–60 sec per side until browned but not grey — don’t overcook. Remove.
Lower heat slightly; add a touch more oil if needed. Stir garlic + ginger ~20 sec. Return broccoli; toss.
Return beef. Pour sauce; toss until thick and glossy, 30–60 sec. Finish with sesame oil. Taste — add soy or sweetener, not heat.
substitutions: No spice: no chili crisp / sriracha / gochujang; flavor from oyster + soy + ginger + garlic.
Lower carb: cauliflower rice; extra broccoli; same beef amount.
Higher protein: 1.25–1.5 lb beef; same sauce.
Sweeteners: stevia / monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup instead of sugar in the sauce — start tiny.
Chicken swap: same method with thinly sliced chicken breast/thigh if you’re in a chicken mood.
notes: Extra lean beef, velvet marinade, stevia instead of sugar, big broccoli, cauliflower rice option.
foodiligence points to a bio recipe we couldn’t pull; this is the standard home-cook beef & broccoli pattern for that Ep 21 title.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate with cauliflower rice ~320–420 kcal · ~35–45g protein · ~12–20g carbs.

title: Chicken & Beef Broccoli (tonight)
imageCredit: Reference stock photo by Zoltan Istella on Pexels (Pexels License)
creator: Chef recommendation (from Mild Beef & Broccoli)
summary: Adapted from Mild Beef & Broccoli — same mild glossy sauce, using both chicken and beef. Spine: Lilly Song meat stir-fry (sear → hold → recombine) + blanch dense broccoli first.
whyItFits: Uses proteins and broccoli already on the shopping list
Same mild oyster-soy glaze — no chili
High protein combo night (~1–1.25 lb total meat)
Fast wok/skillet after a 15-minute velvet rest

items: Beef (~8–10 oz) thin against the grain
Per protein bowl (same marinade twice, or one bowl if cooking immediately): ⅛ tsp baking soda, 1½ tsp low-sodium soy, 1½ tsp water, ½ tsp cornstarch, ½ tsp oil, pinch salt
~1–1.25 lb total meat — high protein. All chicken or all beef also fine.
Pinch stevia or ½–1 tsp 0-sugar syrup
½ tsp sesame oil at the end only

steps: Slice + velvet chicken and beef; rest 15 min. Whisk sauce (no sesame oil yet).
Blanch/microwave broccoli until bright and crisp-tender; drain well.
Screaming hot pan + oil → sear beef in one layer ~45–60 sec/side; remove. Same pan → sear chicken until just opaque/165°F; remove. (Don’t grey them — high heat, fast.)
Lower heat; garlic + ginger ~20 sec. Toss in broccoli.
Return both meats. Pour sauce; toss 30–60 sec until glossy. Sesame oil off heat. Taste — soy/sweetener only, no chili.
substitutions: All chicken or all beef: same sauce and veg path.
Lower carb: cauliflower rice; extra broccoli on the side for volume.
No spice: skip chili crisp / sriracha; oyster + soy + ginger only.
notes: Based on library recipe mild-beef-and-broccoli; techniques meat-stir-fry + dense-veg-stir-fry.
Shopping / fridge check: chicken, beef, broccoli, garlic, ginger, soy/tamari, oyster sauce, cornstarch, baking soda, stevia or 0-sugar syrup; optional cauliflower rice.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Ballpark ~380–480 kcal · ~45–55g protein with cauliflower rice; 3 big servings.
